info.title: vouchfx
info.description: End-to-end integration testing for distributed .NET systems, authored in declarative .e2e.yaml. vouchfx compiles YAML to memory-safe C# via Roslyn, orchestrates the required container topology with .NET Aspire + Testcontainers, and verifies one business transaction across HTTP (REST/SOAP), databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, DynamoDB), message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, Azure Service Bus, Redis Streams), cache/search (Redis, Elasticsearch), S3 object storage, Prometheus metrics, OTLP distributed traces, SMTP capture, webhooks and inline C# — twenty-five providers across eleven step families, with engine-owned RETRY polling, execution-time secret resolution with at-source redaction, and a four-verdict taxonomy where only Fail breaks CI by default.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Discover *.e2e.yaml scenarios under <path> (a directory, or a single *.e2e.yaml file) and run them end-to-end against an orchestrated topology.

options.name: --tag
options.description: Select scenarios whose metadata.tags contains this tag. Repeatable; a scenario matches if it has ANY of the supplied tags (OR).

options.name: --owner
options.description: Select scenarios whose metadata.owner is this value. Repeatable; a scenario matches if its owner is ANY of the supplied owners (OR).

options.name: --path
options.description: Select scenarios whose (normalised) absolute path matches this glob. Supports *, ** and ?; a pattern with no wildcard is matched as a substring.

options.name: --changed-since
options.description: Select only scenarios whose file changed since this git ref (committed diff vs the ref plus the dirty working tree). Requires a git repository.

options.name: --parallel
options.description: Run up to N scenarios concurrently, each owning its OWN container topology (S08). Must be 1 or greater. CAVEAT: each concurrent scenario stands up its own topology, so --parallel N uses up to N times the containers at once. Omit to run sequentially against a single shared topology (the default).

options.name: --watch
options.description: Run once, then watch the .e2e.yaml file and re-run automatically on save, re-using the already-built topology while the `environment` block is unchanged (rebuilding it only when it changes). For local iteration on a single file; press Ctrl-C to stop. Cannot be combined with --parallel. [default: False]

options.name: --fail-on-env-error
options.description: Treat an Environment-error verdict as a CI failure (exit 3). Off by default — only Fail breaks CI. Use this to gate on infrastructure breakage (unhealthy container, image-pull / seed / tunnel failure); the distinct code 3 keeps it separable from a product Fail (1). [default: False]

options.name: --fail-on-inconclusive
options.description: Treat an Inconclusive verdict as a CI failure (exit 4). Off by default — only Fail breaks CI. Use this to gate on results the engine could not decide (timeout, partition outlasted grace, upstream capture unmet); the distinct code 4 keeps it separable from a product Fail (1) and an Environment error (3). [default: False]

options.name: --html
options.description: Write a self-contained HTML report to <path>. Rendered from the same event stream as the terminal output, so the two never disagree. Parent directories are created as needed; an existing file is overwritten. Omit for no HTML report (the default).

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write a JUnit XML results file to <path> for CI ingestion. Rendered from the same event stream as the terminal output; the four verdicts map to distinct JUnit primitives (Fail→failure, Environment-error→error, Inconclusive→skipped). Parent directories are created as needed; an existing file is overwritten. Omit for no JUnit report (the default).

options.name: --events
options.description: Write the raw JSON Lines event stream to the given path. Re-emits the same event stream the terminal / HTML / JUnit reports are rendered from, verbatim — one JSON object per line, UTF-8 without a BOM. Parent directories are created as needed; an existing file is overwritten. Aliased as --json. Omit for no events file (the default).

options.name: --events-stream
options.description: Incrementally append the JSON Lines event stream to <path> in real time as each step and attempt completes (per-step liveness), so a concurrent reader (e.g. `tail -f`) sees lines as they land rather than only after the run finishes. Separate from --events / --json, which still writes once, at the end, byte-for-byte unchanged; the two may be used together or independently. Not wired into --watch. Omit for no incremental events stream (the default).

options.name: --no-decorations
options.description: Render the terminal report as plain text — no ANSI colour and no per-verdict shape glyph — for a screen-reader / CI-friendly view. Off by default; when off, colour + glyph are added only for an interactive TTY with NO_COLOR unset. The verdict text tokens (PASS / FAIL / ENV_ERROR / INCONCLUSIVE) are always shown, so this loses no information. [default: False]

options.name: --no-telemetry
options.description: Opt this run out of anonymous usage telemetry, even if telemetry is enabled. Telemetry is OFF by default and opt-in (vouchfx telemetry enable); set VOUCHFX_NO_TELEMETRY=1 for the same effect in CI / automation. [default: False]

options.name: --shutdown-on-stdin-eof
options.description: Opt in to graceful shutdown on stdin end-of-file: when a host process (e.g. an MCP server) closes this process's redirected standard input, cancel the run and, if it has not finished within the teardown budget, force-exit the process. Off by default; never touches stdin unless set, so behaviour is unchanged for CI / non-interactive runs where stdin is often already at EOF. WARNING: do not combine with a non-interactive or already-closed/redirected-null stdin (e.g. `< /dev/null`) unless a live pipe a host process controls is actually wired up, or the run will cancel immediately. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Directory to search recursively for *.e2e.yaml scenarios, or a single *.e2e.yaml file. Defaults to '.'. [default: .]

commands.name: telemetry
commands.description: Manage opt-in, privacy-first usage telemetry. Telemetry is OFF by default; nothing is collected or sent until you run `telemetry enable`.

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Opt IN to anonymous, aggregate usage telemetry. Mints an install id if one does not exist and confirms the change.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Opt OUT of usage telemetry. Deletes the install id and clears the local outbox immediately.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show the current telemetry consent state, whether an install id exists, the outbox path, and how to opt in / out.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Compile-validate *.e2e.yaml scenarios under <path> (a directory, or a single *.e2e.yaml file) WITHOUT starting any container topology: schema validation, parse/AST build, the provider pipeline's bind/validate/emit, and a Roslyn compile-once. No Docker / Aspire activity occurs.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit a single schema-versioned JSON document to stdout instead of the human-readable report. [default: False]
